substeps.caption: Three cameras on the mobile base, after robot-arms PR 40's cell: one on each end of the cabinet, 0.88 m up, and one on a mast at the back-left corner, 1.75 m up. Each is a Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Wide with its own Pi 5, aimed for good by a printed wedge; the mast's Pi rides in its camera's box, the side cameras' on the cabinet's ends.

The mast camera, from behind and above the arm's shoulder: the whole arm, the presented tray and what the gripper holds, from outside. The wrist camera sees 7-50 cm in front of the gripper, and the bay camera only works here; this one goes to every station with the arm, with the same view every time.

The left side camera, low on the cabinet's end, looking forward past the arm: with the right one, a pair 0.74 m apart that sees the work in front of the arm from 50-60 degrees apart, as robot-arms PR 40's side cameras do (70 there): AprilTags on the station's face, and the gripper's fingertips, in 3-D, before and while the arm moves.

The right side camera: the other half of the pair, and the aisle on this side. All three keep recording through a protective stop: they run on the MiR250's isolated 24 V output, which stays on in an emergency or protective stop (MiR250 electrical interface).

Back out: the vial is on the doser's shuttle and the arm goes home. None of the three is a safety device: the MiR250's scanners and the UR10e's own limits stay the safety functions.
